data.content_ref: inline:The target's stated refutation condition is incoherent relative to the problem. It says the relation is 'refuted if the digit-length function is not stationary within each width-band,' citing leading zeros or mixed radix. But leading zeros and mixed radix are not properties of the page-count problem at all — they are extraneous alternate numbering conventions. The problem asks to connect the isolated artifact to its neighbourhood via a substantive relation; introducing an irrelevant counterfactual numbering system as the *refutation condition* means the condition does not test the proposed relation (reduction to root-finding) but instead tests an unrelated hypothetical. A genuine refutation condition for 'reduces D(n)=N to root-finding' would need to show the function is non-injective or non-monotone within the actual problem domain, not that some imaginary mixed-radix scheme breaks stationarity.
